fields.title: Scoliosis and kyphosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Scoliosis and kyphosis: advanced treatment in Israel

Scoliosis (sideways curvature of the spine) and kyphosis (excessive forward curvature of the spine) are common conditions of the spine that can cause pain, poor posture and, in severe cases, serious functional problems. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive and innovative approach to treating these conditions, including conservative methods, minimally invasive procedures and surgery.

Diagnosis of scoliosis and kyphosis

  1. Clinical examination
    The doctor assesses the degree of curvature of the spine, any visible deformity, restricted movement and other symptoms.
  2. X-rays
    Allow the degree of curvature of the spine to be measured precisely and reveal possible changes in the structure of the vertebrae.
  3. MRI and CT
    Used for detailed imaging of the soft tissues, the intervertebral discs and the nerve structures around the spine.
  4. Laboratory tests
    May be ordered to rule out other conditions contributing to the development of scoliosis or kyphosis.

Treatments in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Physiotherapy: Individually designed exercise programmes to strengthen the supporting muscles and correct the curvature.
    • Wearing a brace: Used to stabilise and correct curvature in children and adolescents during growth.
    • Drug treatment: Prescribed to reduce pain and inflammation.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty: Procedures to restore the height of the vertebrae and relieve pain in compression fractures.
  3. Surgery:
    • Spinal fusion: Surgical fixation of the vertebrae to stabilise the spine and correct the curvature.
    • Laminectomy: Removal of part of a vertebra to relieve pressure on the nerve roots.
    • Fitting of metal implants: Used to hold the spine in the correct position.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • An individualised approach: Every patient is given a personal treatment programme that takes account of the features of their condition and their general health.
  • Advanced technology: The use of the newest methods of diagnosis and treatment, including minimally invasive techniques and innovative surgical methods.
  • A multidisciplinary team: Doctors of various specialities work together to achieve the best treatment results.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation: Recovery programmes after treatment are aimed at returning the patient to normal life quickly.

Treatment of scoliosis and kyphosis in Israel gives patients access to the most modern and effective treatments, with strong prospects of an improvement in their condition and quality of life.

fields.title: Stenting
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Stenting is an advanced, minimally invasive procedure used to restore normal blood flow in narrowed or blocked vessels. It is widely used to treat various vascular conditions, including coronary artery disease (CAD), peripheral artery disease (PAD) and vascular stenoses. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of stenting in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Vascular conditions are usually diagnosed using modern methods that establish the degree of narrowing or blockage of the vessels. These include:

  • Angiography: a procedure in which a contrast medium is introduced into the blood vessels and X-rays are then taken to image the state of the vessels and detect narrowed sections or blockages.
  • Ultrasound scan: ultrasound is used to create images of the vessels and establish their structure and function.
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): MRI provides detailed images of the vessels and helps establish the degree of narrowing or blockage.

Methods of treatment

Stenting is an invasive procedure carried out in an operating theatre or a specialist medical centre. It is performed under local anaesthetic and does not usually require a general anaesthetic. The treatments include:

  • Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI): a procedure in which a flexible tubular stent is introduced into the narrowed section of a coronary artery through a catheter, to restore normal blood flow and prevent further narrowing.
  • Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA): in PTA a special balloon is inflated inside the narrowed vessel, widening it and restoring normal blood flow.
  • Peripheral artery stenting: stents are also used to treat narrowing or blockage in the peripheral arteries, such as those of the legs, in order to restore the blood supply to the limbs.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the leading countries in cardiology and vascular surgery, which makes it an attractive place to have stenting. The advantages of stenting in Israel include:

  • Qualified specialists: Israeli cardiologists and surgeons are highly qualified and have extensive experience in carrying out stenting.
  • Modern technology and equipment: medical institutions in Israel are equipped with advanced devices and technology, which ensures a high level of precision and successful results.
  • An integrated approach to treatment: Israel uses a whole-person approach to the treatment of vascular conditions, which allows patients to be given comprehensive, individual care.

Conclusion

Stenting is an effective and safe treatment for various vascular conditions. The procedure is carried out using advanced technology by experienced specialists in Israel. If you have vascular problems, consult a qualified cardiologist in Israel for the best treatment and the restoration of your health.

fields.title: Tarlatamab
fields.bodyHtml:
An innovative medicine for small cell lung cancer.
In brief: Tarlatamab is a first-in-class bispecific T-cell engager directed at the DLL3 protein, which is expressed on small cell lung cancer (SCLC) cells. It activates the patient's own T lymphocytes and directs them to destroy the tumour cells.

Key features of the medicine

  • Mechanism of action: it binds CD3 on T cells and DLL3 on tumour cells, creating a cytolytic synapse and inducing cell lysis.
  • Indicated in relapsed or progressing extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) after platinum-based chemotherapy.
  • Clinical data: in the phase 2 DeLLphi-301 study, 99 patients showed an objective response rate (ORR) of about 40% and a median duration of response of about 9.7 months.
  • Approved by the US FDA in May 2024.

What to bear in mind during treatment

  • Monitoring is required for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurological toxicity (including immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, ICANS).
  • The medicine is given intravenously with a step-up dosing schedule — for example 1 mg on day 1, 10 mg on days 8 and 15, then every 2 weeks (the dose may be adjusted).
  • For the first infusions, patients need to stay in hospital or a well-equipped cancer centre for the infusion and observation, because of the risk of complications.

What the process looks like for the patient

  1. Preliminary assessment — send in the medical documentation (case history, histology, previous treatment, DLL3 expression, test results).
  2. Consultation with an oncologist and an immunologist, and discussion of suitability and arrangements.
  3. Arrival, first infusions (admission to hospital for observation).
  4. Monitoring for side effects.
  5. Discharge, and a plan for further monitoring and support after treatment.

Cost and estimates

  • This is a high-technology cancer therapy, and the cost is set by an individual estimate (depending on the dose, the length of treatment, accompanying procedures and hospital stay).
  • The estimate covers: the cost of the medicine, the infusion procedures, monitoring (laboratory tests and investigations), hospital admission for the initial doses, and consultations with specialists.
  • Not usually included: accommodation for anyone accompanying the patient, flights, visa costs, and additional supportive treatments if they are not part of the main programme.


Frequently asked questions

Q: Can I have treatment with tarlatamab in Israel?

A: Yes, but only with confirmed small cell lung cancer. The decision is taken by the doctor after reviewing the documentation.

Q: How is the treatment given?

A: The medicine is given intravenously, under observation in hospital because of possible side effects.

Q: When can an effect be seen?

A: In some patients an improvement is seen 2–3 months after treatment begins.

fields.title: Thrombosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Thrombosis: advanced treatment and prevention in Israel

Thrombosis is a condition in which blood clots form in the blood vessels, which can block the flow of blood and lead to serious complications including heart attack and stroke. Israeli medical institutions use modern approaches to the treatment and prevention of thrombosis, based on the latest advances in medical science.

Diagnosis of thrombosis:

  1. Clinical examination and history: The doctor assesses the symptoms and the risk factors for developing thrombosis.
  2. Doppler ultrasound: Allows the blood flow to be assessed and clots in the veins to be detected.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT): Used to diagnose clots in the deep veins and arteries.
  4. Coagulation screen: A laboratory test of blood clotting.

Treatments for thrombosis:

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Anticoagulants: Medicines that prevent new clots forming and existing ones growing.
    • Thrombolytics: Used to dissolve clots that have already formed.
    • Anti-inflammatory medicines: To reduce inflammation and pain around the clot.
  2. Surgery:
    • Thrombectomy: Removal of the clot from the vessel.
    • Fitting a vena cava filter in the inferior vena cava to prevent clots travelling from the legs to the lungs.
  3. Compression therapy: Wearing compression stockings to improve the flow of blood in the veins and prevent clots forming.
  4. Physiotherapy: Specific exercises to improve blood flow and prevent thrombosis.

Prevention of thrombosis:

  • An active lifestyle: Regular exercise to stimulate the circulation.
  • Diet: A diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids and low in saturated fats, to keep the blood vessels healthy.
  • Avoiding long periods of inactivity: Regular breaks to move about during long journeys or sedentary work.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Specialists from various fields of medicine work together to create an individual treatment plan for every patient.
  • Access to innovative treatments: The use of the latest medical developments and medicines.
  • Modern diagnostic technology: Ensuring accurate diagnosis and monitoring of patients' condition.
  • A comprehensive approach to prevention: The development of individual recommendations on lifestyle changes to reduce the risk of thrombosis.

Treatment and prevention of thrombosis in Israel is carried out through integrated programmes aimed at minimising the risk of complications and improving patients' general health.
